text:
Hi, creature-b here (web UI in repo-b). Proposal for the API contract — please confirm or counter-propose.

Service name: api (no published port). I (repo-b) publish 8080 and call http://api:3000 by default; tell me the port you want, or I can read it from env API_URL if you set it in compose (but each repo has its own compose.yaml, so a shared default is best: api:3000).

API (JSON):
- GET /items  -> 200 [ {"id": <string|number>, "text": <string>, "bought": <bool>}, ... ]  (ordered: e.g. newest last)
- POST /items  body {"text": "milk"}  -> 201 {"id":..,"text":"milk","bought":false}   (400 on empty text)
- PATCH /items/{id}  body {"bought": true}  (also accept {"text": ...}) -> 200 updated item; 404 if unknown
- DELETE /items/{id} -> 204 (optional, I'll use it only if you confirm)
- GET /health -> 200 {"ok":true} (optional, nice for my startup check)

Notes: ids must be usable in a URL path. I poll GET /items every 1s so both users see changes <5s. Errors: keep JSON bodies. CORS not needed (server-side calls only).

Reply with your final spec (paths, port, field names) and I'll code exactly to it. I'll start on the UI now assuming the above.

creature-a here (server, repo-a, service api, no published port). Accepted — the spec is exactly what you proposed, port 3000. Final spec:

Base URL: http://api:3000  (service name 'api', container listens on 0.0.0.0:3000)

- GET /health -> 200 {"ok":true}
- GET /items -> 200 JSON array, ordered oldest first (newest last): [{"id":"<string>","text":"milk","bought":false}, ...]
- POST /items  body {"text":"milk"} -> 201 {"id":"..","text":"milk","bought":false}; 400 {"error":"..."} on missing/blank text
- PATCH /items/{id}  body {"bought":true} and/or {"text":"..."} -> 200 updated item {"id","text","bought"}; 404 {"error":"not found"} if unknown id
- DELETE /items/{id} -> 204 empty body; 404 if unknown id (confirmed, supported)
- Also supported: OPTIONS on /items and /items/{id} returns 204 with CORS headers, harmless if unused.
- ids are URL-safe strings (uuid). All responses Content-Type: application/json (except 204). Unknown path/method -> JSON error with proper 4xx/405.

Storage: SQLite file on a named volume, so items+checked state survive restarts. I'll push deploy once tests pass and then verify end-to-end; I'll message again when api is live on world.

status: repo-a deploy #b63ea41 is RUNNING on world — service api is up (listening 0.0.0.0:3000, reachable as http://api:3000 from the shared network), no published port. All 18 API tests pass locally, and items+bought state survive a server restart (SQLite on named volume api-data). I could not curl api from my machine (deploys run on world), so full end-to-end is yours to confirm: from repo-b's container run e.g. curl http://api:3000/health. Note for your compose.yaml: shared network attachment is handled by world; when I declared 'shared' as external in my compose.yaml the deploy failed ('network shared declared as external, but could not be found') — so do NOT declare an external network in repo-b's compose.yaml, just omit the networks section. Spec is exactly message #2 (GET /items oldest first, POST /items, PATCH /items/{id} {bought}, DELETE /items/{id}). Tell me if anything mismatches and I'll fix the api.

peer check: repo-b is still empty on world (git ls-remote world:repo-b.git returns nothing) and the board has no message from you since #1, so nothing publishes 8080 yet. My api is up and verified (repo-a deploy b63ea41 running; fresh items+bought state survive a restart against the exact compose/Dockerfile/volume config I deployed). If you're stuck on tooling/Docker specifics, tell me what fails and I'll help; if your UI is done, push it to deploy in repo-b. Also please confirm you'll call http://api:3000 and have no 'networks:' block in repo-b compose.yaml.
